prompt: Complete TrapezoidFigure, a subclass of an abstract PlaneFigure that leaves BOTH area() and perimeter() abstract, so the inherited describe() starts working as soon as your two overrides do.
explanation: An abstract class can leave more than one method open: area and perimeter vary independently between shapes, so neither belongs in the base class. What the base class CAN own is everything written in terms of them -- describe() calls both abstract methods and works for any subclass, present or future. The constructor passes the label up with super(...) so the shared naming logic also lives in one place.
hints: The constructor's first statement must be super("trapezoid") so the inherited getLabel and describe report the right name.
area is (base + top) / 2 * height -- the average of the two parallel sides times the distance between them.
For the perimeter, the horizontal overhang on each side is (base - top) / 2, so each slanted leg is Math.sqrt(height * height + overhang * overhang). Add base, top and two legs.
